question.text: Per SEBI's framework, if a Cat II AIF's valuation of a single investee asset deviates by more than a certain percentage between two consecutive valuations OR more than another percentage in a financial year, the Investment Manager must inform investors with detailed reasons. These thresholds are:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.12: 'At each asset level, in case of deviation in valuation of more than 20% between two consecutive valuations or a deviation of more than 33% in a financial year, the Investment Manager shall inform the investors with reasons.' This is a bright-line disclosure trigger. The Trap: 10/20 is too tight; 25/50 is too loose; 33/20 inverts the two numbers. Remember the formula: '20% consecutive, 33% annual' — a useful mnemonic is '2-3' (20-33). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same thresholds. XIX-A tests them from a distributor/investor disclosure angle. This is a hot inspection topic post the Sep 2024 framework. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a valuation-deviation tracker in your fund-admin system that auto-flags any asset crossing 20% QoQ or 33% YTD. Your IC should review the flagged assets before investor communication goes out.
